text:
Nina: Brief: canary warmup stalled on gzipped safetensors. Symptoms: repeated 206 range hits and checksum mismatches, no OOM.
storage-bot: [alert] warmup.read_spike shard=lm-large-0006
Theo: logs?
Nina: snippet:
```
2026-04-12T08:15:10Z fetch range 0-65535 -> 206
2026-04-12T08:15:10Z verify post-decompress expected=9a8b got=0000
2026-04-12T08:15:10Z retry backoff=40ms
```
Rashmi: Sounds like range cuts a gzip header. We're verifying after decompression today.
Theo: Quick fixes: (A) bump initial prime to 128k, (B) on checksum fail run a single elastic prime (e.g., 512k) before giving up, (C) add compressed_digest in manifest so loader can verify compressed bytes first.
Nina: I ran (B) on a micro-canary; stalls went away and bandwidth impact was minimal.
Rashmi: Agree on manifest: add `compression: "gzip"` and optional `compressed_sha256`. Loader behavior: if compressed_sha256 present -> verify compressed bytes first; else -> use elastic-prime fallback.
Theo: Add metrics: loader.gz_checksum_mismatch, loader.gz_elastic_primes, loader.gz_compressed_verify_fail tagged by model/shard/region.
Nina: Tests: unit for partial-gzip stream, integration with an HTTP stub that serves split ranges, canary rollout with telemetry checks.
Rashmi: Long-term: sidecar index with per-compressed-chunk checksums to avoid large primes.
Theo: Action items: Rashmi -> manifest PR and metrics; Nina -> RFC follow-up + rollout plan; I'll own loader PR and tests.
Nina: creating ticket INF-9812 "gzip header-split elastic prime + compressed-digest" and will link PRs. Thanks.
